newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman group in $300mln BOOT Salalah wastewater deal.
newsitem.headline: Oman group in $300mln BOOT Salalah wastewater deal.

text.p: A group of Omani businessmen expect to sign by mid-November a $300 million build own operate transfer (BOOT) contract to set up and manage Oman's first major sewerage network, a group spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We are in the final negotiating stage and are awaiting the signing with the government, which we hope will be by mid-November," Thamer bin Saeed al-Shanfari told Reuters.
He said the new Salalah Environmental Treatment Co (SETCO), which is under formation, was awarded the contract in July to build the plant, to which 20,000 homes will be connected in southern Oman.
Shanfari will be chairman of SETCO once it is formally established.
"The total project cost over a 30-year period will be approximately $300 million," he said.
Shanfari said the Salalah project will be Oman's first major sewerage treatment plant and network. A similar project, Muscat Wastewater, is also planned for the capital.
Analysts say BOOT contracts are set to become more popular in the Gulf, where states are trying to give the private sector a bigger role in their oil- and government-dominated economies.
Under a BOOT scheme, the developer owns the plant and collects the revenue for a fixed period and then hands it back to the state.
The Salalah plant will be Oman's second BOOT project after the Manah power station near Nizwa, which in April became the Gulf's first infrastructure project carried out using the BOOT formula.

Shanfari said construction was likely to start in Salalah in early 1997. Britain's Costain Group Plc will handle the construction management and the technical operator will be Northwest Water International, part of United Utilities Plc of Britain.
The two firms will take equity in the project, along with Omani partners led by the Shanfari Group.
Forty-nine percent of the new company's capital of 10 million rials ($26 million) will then be floated to the public.
"We hope it will go onto the (Muscat) stock market about three months after we sign with the government," Shanfari said.
